title: Insulin Physiology and Acute Complications of Diabetes Mellitus

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: The islets of Langerhans are written as what percentage of pancreatic volume?
questions.exp: The formation note says islets of Langerhans are 2% of pancreatic volume. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Insulin is written as a polypeptide of ___ amino acids.
questions.exp: The formation note identifies insulin as a polypeptide of 51 amino acids. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Match the insulin physiology item to its printed description — 1) Formation site 2) Structure 3) Receptor 4) Exception … A) Islets of Langerhans B) Chains connected by disulphide bonds C) Tyrosine kinase D) TGF-β uses serine-threonine kinase
questions.exp: The page gives islets of Langerhans, chains joined by disulphide bonds, a tyrosine-kinase receptor, and TGF-β as the serine-threonine-kinase exception. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Assess the receptor note: I Insulin acts via a tyrosine-kinase receptor. II TGF-β is listed as an exception using a serine-threonine-kinase pathway.
questions.exp: Both receptor statements are written in the physiology notes. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Which tissue is included in the page's insulin-dependent GLUT-4 glucose uptake list?
questions.exp: The GLUT-4 uptake list names skeletal muscle, adipose tissue and heart. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Match the insulin effect to the carbohydrate-metabolism entry — 1) Glucose uptake 2) Glucose production 3) Gluconeogenesis 4) Glycogenolysis … A) Via GLUT-4 in muscle, adipose tissue and heart B) Regulated by insulin C) Decreased D) Decreased
questions.exp: The page shows insulin-dependent GLUT-4 uptake, regulation of glucose production, and negative effects on gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: The page links increased glucose production to hyperglycemia and then to which pair through osmotic diuresis?
questions.exp: The flow below increased glucose production reads hyperglycemia followed by polyuria and polydipsia through osmotic diuresis. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the infections specifically labelled as diabetic-mellitus specific?
questions.exp: The page lists mucormycosis, emphysematous cholecystitis, emphysematous pyelonephritis and malignant otitis externa; meningitis is not in that bracket. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: The protein-metabolism section links decreased amino-acid uptake to ___.
questions.exp: The page shows decreased amino-acid uptake leading to weakness. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Assess the protein-metabolism notes: I Decreased amino-acid synthesis is linked to infections. II Increased proteolysis is linked to wasting.
questions.exp: Both arrows are shown in the protein-metabolism section. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: Which metabolism is listed after carbohydrate and protein metabolism at the bottom of the page?
questions.exp: The third numbered section is fat metabolism and it notes lipolysis. (Book p927)

questions.sec: Physiology of insulin
questions.q: In the insulin-production diagram, what event follows ATP/ADP-related closure of the ATP-sensitive potassium channel?
questions.exp: The production diagram shows ATP/ADP, the ATP-sensitive K+ channel, depolarization and voltage-gated calcium-channel involvement before secretion. (Book p927)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Match the transporter to the tissue location — 1) GLUT1 2) GLUT2 3) GLUT3 4) GLUT4 … A) Brain, kidney, colon, placenta, erythrocyte B) Liver, pancreatic beta cell, small intestine, kidney C) Brain, kidney, placenta D) Heart, skeletal muscle, adipose tissue
questions.exp: The GLUT table gives the listed tissue distributions for GLUT1, GLUT2, GLUT3 and GLUT4. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Which transporter is marked as insulin-stimulated uptake of glucose?
questions.exp: The GLUT4 row states insulin-stimulated uptake of glucose. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: The small-intestine transporter that takes up fructose is ___.
questions.exp: The GLUT5 row lists small intestine and uptake of fructose. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Assess the transporter table: I SGLT1 is in small intestine and actively takes up glucose from the lumen. II SGLT2 reabsorbs glucose in the proximal convoluted tubule of the kidney.
questions.exp: Both SGLT rows carry those tissue and function labels. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Match the glucose/C-peptide pattern to the associated condition — 1) C-peptide undetectable, glucose increased 2) C-peptide increased, glucose increased 3) C-peptide increased, glucose decreased 4) C-peptide decreased, glucose decreased … A) T1DM B) T2DM C) Insulinoma D) Exogenous insulin
questions.exp: The table pairs undetectable C-peptide/increased glucose with T1DM, increased/increased with T2DM, increased/decreased with insulinoma, and decreased/decreased with exogenous insulin. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: A patient has low glucose, low C-peptide and a history suggesting administered insulin. Which association is printed?
questions.exp: The C-peptide table associates decreased C-peptide and decreased glucose with exogenous insulin. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: How many incretin hormones are branched from the word 'incretins' in the diagram?
questions.exp: The diagram branches incretins to GLP-1 and GIP, making two hormones. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: The incretin effect augments insulin production in response to which type of meal entry named on the page?
opts: A protein meal entering the colon
A saline meal entering the ileum
A fat meal entering the stomach
questions.exp: The note says incretins augment insulin production in response to a glucose meal, written as intrajejunal glucose. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Which recombinant GLP-1 application is written as not easily degraded by DPP-4?
opts: Recombinant GLP-1 used in treatment of DM
questions.exp: The applied-aspect note names recombinant GLP-1 for DM and says it is not easily degraded by DPP-4. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Assess the applied-aspect list: I Exenatide is annotated with pancreatitis risk. II Liraglutide is written as subcutaneous.
questions.exp: The page lists exenatide with pancreatitis risk and liraglutide s/c. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Match the applied drug to the page's note — 1) Exenatide 2) Liraglutide 3) Semaglutide 4) Tirzepatide … A) Pancreatitis risk B) Subcutaneous C) Oral with increased weight loss D) Dual GLP-1/GIP analogue
questions.exp: The application list gives exenatide with pancreatitis risk, liraglutide s/c, oral semaglutide with increased weight loss, and tirzepatide as a dual GLP-1/GIP analogue. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin hormones
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the abbreviated hormones or transporters explicitly written in the incretin section?
questions.exp: GLP-1, GIP and DPP-4 appear in this page's incretin notes; cortisol does not. (Book p928)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Match the incretin to its source — 1) GLP-1 2) GIP … A) L cells of ileum and colon B) K cells of jejunum
questions.exp: The table gives GLP-1 from L cells of ileum and colon and GIP from K cells of jejunum. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Assess the first GLP-1 versus GIP rows: I Both have +++ glucose-dependent insulin release. II Both have +++ enhancement of beta-cell glucose responsiveness.
questions.exp: Both columns show +++ for glucose-dependent insulin release and for enhancement of beta-cell glucose responsiveness. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Which incretin column has +++ suppression of glucagon release?
questions.exp: The table shows +++ under GLP-1 and dashes under GIP for suppression of glucagon release. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Match the listed effect to the stronger incretin column — 1) Stimulates beta-cell expansion 2) Inhibits gastric emptying 3) Enhances satiety 4) Reduces body weight … A) GLP-1 B) GLP-1 C) GLP-1 D) GLP-1
questions.exp: For each of these rows the GLP-1 column is marked +++ while GIP has dashes. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: What half-life is written for GLP-1 in the table?
questions.exp: The GLP-1 half-life row states 1–2 minutes and notes rapid degradation by DPP-4. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: The GIP half-life in the table is written as ___ minutes.
questions.exp: The GIP half-life row reads 5–7 minutes. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Which page-listed feature supports choosing recombinant GLP-1 over another hypoglycemic agent?
questions.exp: The advantages list includes no risk of hypoglycemia, weight loss, cardio-protection, HbA1c reduction and nephroprotection. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: The page says recombinant GLP-1 is used in treatment of which liver-fat condition?
questions.exp: The advantages list says recombinant GLP-1 promotes weight loss and is used in treatment of NASH/NAFLD. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Assess the nephron note: I Adult diabetes is associated with nephron underdosing. II Low birth weight is linked to decreased nephron number in Bartter’s theory.
questions.exp: The note links adult diabetes with nephron underdosing, low birth weight, decreased nephron number and Bartter’s theory. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Match the insulin-deficiency complication group to its examples — 1) Acute 2) Chronic 3) Macrovascular … A) DKA and HHS B) Retinopathy, nephropathy and peripheral neuropathy C) Atherosclerotic CVD and CKD
questions.exp: The complication diagram lists DKA/HHS under acute, retinopathy/nephropathy/peripheral neuropathy under chronic, and atherosclerotic CVD/CKD under macrovascular. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the acute complications listed under insulin deficiency?
questions.exp: Retinopathy is in the chronic column; DKA and HHS are listed in the acute column. (Book p929)

questions.sec: GLP-1 versus GIP and complications of insulin deficiency
questions.q: Which precipitating factor for DKA appears in the right-hand list?
questions.exp: The DKA precipitating-factor list includes cocaine and non-compliance to treatment. (Book p929)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Match the DKA pathophysiology step to the next printed step — 1) Absolute insulin deficiency 2) Increased CPT-1 3) Free fatty acids 4) Acetyl-CoA … A) With counter-regulatory hormones B) Lipolysis and beta-oxidation in mitochondria C) Undergo beta-oxidation D) Increased ketone-body formation
questions.exp: The flow begins with absolute insulin deficiency and counter-regulatory hormones, increased CPT-1, free-fatty-acid beta-oxidation, acetyl-CoA formation and ketone bodies. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Free fatty acids undergo ___ in the mitochondria in the DKA flowchart.
questions.exp: The DKA diagram states that free fatty acids undergo beta-oxidation in mitochondria. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Assess the DKA flow: I Increased acetyl-CoA formation precedes ketone-body formation. II The endpoint shown is ketosis/ketoacidosis.
questions.exp: Both arrows are visible in the DKA pathophysiology sequence. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: In the comparison written at the top of the page, absolute insulin deficiency is greater in which direction?
questions.exp: The page annotates absolute insulin deficiency as T1DM >> T2DM. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: A child with DKA is being monitored for the page's highlighted complication associated with increased mortality. What is it?
questions.exp: The note states that cerebral edema is seen in children and increases mortality. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Match the DKA clinical item to the printed category — 1) Nausea/vomiting 2) Respiratory distress out of proportion to lung signs 3) Fruity odour 4) High-anion-gap metabolic acidosis … A) Symptom B) Sign C) Acidotic breath sign D) Investigation finding
questions.exp: The page places nausea/vomiting under symptoms, respiratory distress under signs, fruity odour under acidotic breath, and HAGMA under investigations. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Which symptom is listed alongside thirst/polyuria in DKA?
questions.exp: The symptoms list includes nausea/vomiting, thirst/polyuria, abdominal pain and shortness of breath. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the DKA signs listed on the page?
questions.exp: The signs list dehydration, tachycardia, respiratory distress, acidotic breath and abdominal tenderness; bradycardia is not listed. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Match the investigation to the exact DKA investigation list — 1) ABG 2) Beta-hydroxybutyrate 3) Urine 4) Blood tests … A) HAGMA B) Level C) Ketones D) CBC, RFT and serum electrolytes
questions.exp: The investigation list includes ABG showing HAGMA, beta-hydroxybutyrate level, urine ketones, CBC, RFT and serum electrolytes. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Abdominal tenderness in this DKA page is noted as requiring a differential diagnosis of:
questions.exp: The page annotates abdominal tenderness with differential diagnosis of acute pancreatitis. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: Assess the counter-regulatory-hormone note: I Glucagon, epinephrine and cortisol are named. II Proteolysis increases gluconeogenic substrates.
questions.exp: The page names glucagon, epinephrine and cortisol and draws proteolysis leading to increased gluconeogenic substrates. (Book p930)

questions.sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations
questions.q: The right-hand DKA flow runs from uncontrolled hyperglycemia through osmotic diuresis to ECF volume ___.
questions.exp: The page's right-hand flow ends osmotic diuresis followed by ECF volume depletion. (Book p930)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: The DKA fluid ladder begins by replacing approximately what total volume?
questions.exp: The DKA treatment note says fluids replace 6–9 L. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: Match the DKA fluid stage to the printed timing — 1) First 3 L 2) Second 3 L 3) Third 3 L … A) Over 3 hours B) Over 9 hours C) Over 12 hours
questions.exp: The fluid ladder is 3 L over 3 hours, 3 L over 9 hours and 3 L over 12 hours. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: For every litre of DKA fluid, the note gives one ampoule of KCl containing:
questions.exp: The page states one amp KCl, 10 mL equal to 20 mEq, for every 1 L fluid after the insulin stat dose. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: The regular-insulin stat dose written for DKA is 0.1 U/kg ___.
questions.exp: The DKA treatment line specifies regular insulin stat dose 0.1 U/kg IV. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: After the DKA regular-insulin stat dose, what infusion rate is written?
questions.exp: The page gives a regular-insulin infusion of 0.1 U/kg/hr after the stat dose. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: Assess the glucose-monitoring instruction: I Blood glucose is monitored every hour. II At 200 mg/dL, fluids switch from normal saline to 5% dextrose.
questions.exp: The DKA treatment box says monitor blood glucose every hour and switch from NS to 5% dextrose at 200 mg/dL. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: A 50-kg patient is being treated using the page's example. What hourly insulin rate is written first in the example?
questions.exp: The example converts 0.1 U/kg/hr for a 50-kg patient to 5 U/hr first. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: The DKA section gives what prognosis?
questions.exp: The prognosis line after the DKA treatment ladder says good. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: Match the HHS feature to the printed note — 1) Insulin deficiency 2) Patient group 3) Precipitating factor example 4) Time course … A) Relative, T2DM > T1DM B) Elderly patient C) LRTI D) One week
questions.exp: HHS is described as relative insulin deficiency (T2DM > T1DM), in an elderly patient, with LRTI as an example precipitant, developing over a week. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: Assess the HHS pathophysiology: I Mildly increased counter-regulatory hormones are shown. II Ketosis and acidosis are shown as present.
questions.exp: HHS shows a mild counter-regulatory-hormone increase and explicitly says no ketosis/acidosis. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: The HHS flowchart ends with increased fluid loss followed by ___.
questions.exp: The printed sequence is hyperglycemia, osmotic diuresis, hyperosmolarity, increased fluid loss and comatose. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA treatment and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the HHS flowchart steps?
questions.exp: The HHS diagram includes proteolysis, gluconeogenesis and hyperosmolarity but specifically notes no ketosis/acidosis; ketone-body formation is not a step. (Book p931)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: Match the laboratory item to the DKA value shown in the table — 1) Glucose 2) Serum sodium 3) Osmolality 4) Plasma ketones … A) 350–1000 mg/dL B) 125–135 mEq/L C) 300–320 mOsm/mL D) ++++
questions.exp: The DKA column gives glucose 350–1000, serum sodium 125–135, osmolality 300–320 and plasma ketones ++++. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: What glucose value is printed for HHS in the DKA-versus-HHS table?
questions.exp: The HHS glucose row is written as >800 mg/dL. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: The HHS serum-sodium range is 135–145 mEq/L, so the table notes that ___ normal saline is used.
questions.exp: The sodium row annotates the HHS 135–145 range with therefore 1/2 NS used. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: Assess the ketone and pH rows: I DKA plasma ketones are ++++. II HHS pH is written as normal.
questions.exp: The table shows ++++ plasma ketones for DKA and normal pH for HHS. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: Match the table finding to its DKA direction — 1) Bicarbonate 2) pH 3) PCO2 4) Anion gap … A) Decreased B) Decreased C) Decreased D) Increased
questions.exp: The DKA column shows decreased bicarbonate, pH and PCO2, with an increased anion gap. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: A patient has HHS with moderate creatinine increase attributed to fluid loss. Which renal consequence is written beside it?
questions.exp: The HHS creatinine cell reads moderate increase with increased fluid loss leading to prerenal failure. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: The first fluid instruction for HHS is slow fluid correction using:
questions.exp: HHS management begins with slow fluid correction using 1/2 NS. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: The HHS management note replaces approximately what volume over 4–5 days?
questions.exp: The page says replace 12 L over 4–5 days, approximately 3 L/day. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: Assess the insulin transition: I IV insulin is shifted to subcutaneous insulin when the patient is awake and taking fluids. II The page says to stop insulin before the patient can drink.
questions.exp: The management arrow says IV insulin, when awake and taking fluids, shifts to subcutaneous insulin. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: Match the subcutaneous insulin item to the printed schedule — 1) Regular insulin 2) Long-acting insulin 3) Ultra-long-acting insulin 4) Normal body production … A) 8 U–8 U–8 U B) Glargine/detemir daily C) Degludec once in two days D) 40 U
questions.exp: The overlap note writes 40 U normal production, regular 8–8–8, glargine/detemir daily and degludec once in two days. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: What prognosis is written at the end of the HHS section?
questions.exp: The final prognosis line on the page reads relatively poor. (Book p932)

questions.sec: DKA versus HHS laboratory values and management
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the analytes marked normal in the HHS column?
questions.exp: Potassium, magnesium and chloride are marked normal in HHS; plasma ketones are marked ±, not ++++. (Book p932)
